chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Taking up the lower-register clarinet on 'Cabin in the Cotton'
summary: On April 28, 1932 Irving Mills rejected the written arrangement until Holmes noodled the melody on low clarinet, which Mills wanted.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay, so tell me about... One of the recording dates, April 28, 1932.
Oh yeah. I remember it like it was yesterday. 1932. Hmm, this is...
So the tune was "Cabin In The Cotton." What happened?

Well, we had an arrangement on the number, a very nice, dignified arrangement. And the clarinets played together, the saxophones played together, the brass and everything was together. It sounded beautiful. But it wasn't what the man wanted. He couldn't explain what he wanted.

Yeah. He couldn't explain what he wanted, but he didn't want that. So I just happened to be foolin' around with the clarinet in the lower register, and I got to playing the melody on the number, you know, put a little (?) in there, one of those things, to kind of jazz it up a little bit.
